title: Native prime-field factor-base size and decomposition-oracle tuning
status_note: Protocol frozen 2026-10-29 (PROTOCOL.md §12): ecbench compare --weight on main resolves blocker 1; random-base control absent and recorded as a gap; plan check at code.commit reproduces the incumbent ids, 232/232/208/208 train executions and fresh curves. No session has run.
question: Can joint selection of factor-base size and exact native decomposition oracle reduce complete one-target IC cost against the current verified prime-field incumbent on fresh matched workloads?
decision_value: A verified holdout reduction robust to the common native-operation pricing band promotes the selected recipe to the next IC baseline, even if rho is still cheaper. A null, failed or price-sensitive result retains the incumbent and narrows the tuning question; no coverage-only result is promoted to a pipeline improvement.

resources.notes: Derived in README.md from measured per-run walls (frontier Phase 1 sessions; this card's probes A-C): ~50 min of one core for identity, train (+edge extensions), holdout, panel K, replay-all audit and analysis, plus ~20 min for outputs.verify; 2 core-hours / 2 wall-hours include ~2x margin for a contended spot host. Peak process RSS ~0.66 GiB (mitm m=3, N=4096, 32 bits); ~30 MB of session records. Estimates, not measurements.

outputs.result_schema: ecbench sessions (ecbench.record/v1) under {out}/sessions, replay-all receipts under {out}/audits, xp-pbo.selection/v1 + FROZEN.sha256 under {out}/select, ecbench.band/v1 and compare JSON under {out}/analysis (PROTOCOL.md section 13)

cairn.notes: Frozen; not yet published or leased. One sequential shard; resumable at session granularity by rerunning the same command (--resume).
